fig1_claim_protein_divergence: Fig. 1 | Protein divergence within S. cerevisiae, within Saccharomyces and within mammals on one axis. Each point is a pair; the y axis is 100 minus protein identity (log scale, inverted; identity on the right). Within S. cerevisiae (n = 1,011 isolates): the mean over S288C reference ORFs of each isolate's protein identity to S288C, from Peter 2018's reference-inferred alleles, with every gap column of a frameshifted or indel-bearing ORF charged (06_isolate_protein_identity.py); the per-isolate MEDIAN over ORFs, which frameshifted ORFs do not pull down, gives a median divergence of 0.28%. Every other column: AAI, the mean percent identity over reciprocal best mmseqs2 hits of one-protein-per-gene proteomes (03_mmseqs_rbh.py); n pairs per column Within Saccharomyces 3, Within mammals 28, Mammal vs chicken 8, Within Saccharomycotina 75, Within bacteria 45, Saccharomycotina vs bacteria 130. Open diamonds: AAI restricted to Eukaryota-level eggNOG OGs that are single copy in both members, the proxy for Peris et al. 2023's BUSCO AAI. Point face and edge colors are the taxonomic groups of the two members. Gray band: one human genome differs from GRCh38 at 10,000 to 12,000 peptide-altering sites (1000 Genomes Project 2015, doi:10.1038/nature15393; literature value, not computed here), divided by this study's 11.7 million-residue human per-gene proteome.
fig2_cladogram_heatmaps: Fig. 2 | The organisms torchcell serves or targets on three similarity axes, ordered by the NCBI taxonomy. Left: NCBI taxonomy cladogram (topology only; ete3 NCBITaxa, 05_trees.py) of the 34 reference organisms; the strip is the plan's first group per organism. Heatmaps, rows and columns in cladogram order: AAI (mean percent identity over reciprocal best hits, 03_mmseqs_rbh.py), ortholog Jaccard (RBH count over the union of the two per-gene proteomes) and EC-4 Jaccard (complete EC numbers from one eggNOG-mapper 2 run, eggNOG 5.0.2, 04_emapper.py). Gray: no proteome (A. limacinum has no annotated assembly at NCBI) or the diagonal.
fig3_taxonomy_vs_aai_nj: Fig. 3 | NCBI taxonomy and AAI agree on the large groups. Left: NCBI taxonomy cladogram (topology only) over the 33 organisms with a proteome. Right: neighbor-joining tree (Biopython) on d = -ln(AAI/100), rooted with the bacteria as outgroup, drawn as topology with children rotated to follow the left tree. Lines join the same organism and are colored by its taxonomic group (05_trees.py).
fig4_clade_tree_within_distance: Fig. 4 | Every named S. cerevisiae clade but one is tighter than the species as a whole. (a) Neighbor-joining tree (Biopython) over the 30 groups of Peter et al. 2018's 1,011 isolates: the 29 clades of their Supplementary Table 1 (Wine/European subclades merged) and the 49 isolates the table gives no clade; the distance between two groups is the mean SNP distance (percent non-identical bases, heterozygous differences half-weighted) over every pair of their members, midpoint rooted, branch lengths in percent. Bold leaf and black dot: the clade holding ADT, the isolate with the lowest mean per-ORF nucleotide divergence from S288C in experiment 018 (0.0005%); S288C itself is not in Peter's matrix. (b) SNP distance between every pair of isolates within a group, same rows. 27 of the 28 named clades with at least one pair have a median below the median over all 510,555 isolate pairs (1.02%, dashed gray line); clade medians run from 0.0015% (22. Far East Russian) to 1.03% (M3. Mosaic region 3), median 0.44%. Boxes (groups with at least 10 pairs): median, quartiles and whiskers at one and a half times the interquartile range, outliers not drawn; points: every pair of a smaller group. One color for every group, since color carries no category here. Log axis.
fig5_ortholog_fraction_vs_aai: Fig. 5 | Shared orthologs fall with AAI. Each point is one of the 528 pairs of the 33 proteomes: AAI, the mean percent identity over reciprocal best mmseqs2 hits, against the ortholog fraction, the number of reciprocal best hits over the gene count of the smaller per-gene proteome (03_mmseqs_rbh.py). Color is the pair class (n pairs in the legend; amniote is a mammal or the chicken); a within-group class takes that group's Fig. 1 color, and a cross-group class takes a color no group uses. Points are drawn largest class first; the cross-kingdom pairs at the lowest AAI overlap. Within Saccharomyces 3, Within mammals 28, Mammal vs chicken 8, Within Saccharomycotina 75, Within bacteria 45, Saccharomycotina vs bacteria 130, Saccharomycotina vs amniote 117, Amniote vs bacteria 90, R. toruloides vs Saccharomycotina 13, R. toruloides vs amniote 9, R. toruloides vs bacteria 10.
fig6_main_transfer_ladder: Fig. 6 | The training isolates reach human/chimp protein divergence from S288C; P. kudriavzevii SD108 lies beyond every vertebrate pair, with 59.5% of its genes in one-to-one orthology with S. cerevisiae. (a) Protein divergence from S288C (100 minus identity, log scale, inverted; identity on the right), columns left to right by distance, colored by the partner's taxonomic group. The 1,011 isolates are drawn twice: each isolate's median over ORFs of protein identity to S288C (circles; median over isolates 99.72%) and its mean over ORFs, which charges every gap column of a frameshifted or indel-bearing ORF (triangles; median 98.04%, lowest 95.55%, against human/chimp AAI 98.14%). SD108 (large point, black edge) is at 47.1% AAI from S288C, below the lowest of the 36 vertebrate pairs (71.5%; human/chicken 72.1%); the other Saccharomycotina hosts sit at 46.4 to 59.2%, the mammals and chicken at 41.0 to 41.4% and the bacteria at 35.1 to 37.0%. Right of the dashed line, the same axis measured from human, as a yardstick (mammals blue, chicken gray). Gray band: one human genome vs GRCh38 at peptide-altering sites (1000 Genomes 2015, literature value). (b) Ortholog fraction with S288C, reciprocal best hits over the smaller per-gene proteome, same organisms and order as (a) without the isolates. SD108 shares 3,072 reciprocal best hits with S288C, 59.5% of its 5,159 genes; the other Saccharomycotina range from 0.410 to 0.868, no bacterium exceeds 0.111. AAI: mean percent identity over reciprocal best mmseqs2 hits (03_mmseqs_rbh.py); isolate identity: 06_isolate_protein_identity.py; table: results/s288c_centered.csv.
